title: Aortic Stiffness Estimated by Oscillometric Methods and Progression of Kidney Damage in Hypertensive Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease
content: Background/Objectives– The aim of our study was to evaluate the potential relationship between increased aortic stiffness measured by oscillometric device and the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in a group of hypertensive patients with chronic kidney disease. Materials and Methods – 395 patients were enrolled between January 2011 and December 2020 and underwent routine biochemical blood tests, clinical blood pressure measurement, ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, and estimation of aortic stiffness. Data regarding the progression of kidney disease were also recorded. Results – The entire population was divided into two groups based on the threshold value of PWV of 10 m/s. Patients in the group with PWV > 10 m/s showed significantly higher levels of pulse pressure, uric acid, and age, and a significantly lower eGFR compared to the group with PWV ≤ 10 m/s. In multivariate analysis using Cox regression, PWV predicted a rapid decline in renal function, independently of eGFR, age, smoking status, sex, and blood pressure values (HR 1.784, CI 1.164-2.734, P=0.0082). 9.99 m/s was the best cut-off value, obtained using the Youden index, to discriminate progressors from non-progressors, Conclusions – Our study, the first conducted using an oscillometric device for stiffness estimation, confirms findings from existing literature, highlighting the importance of PWV in risk stratification for hypertensive patients with chronic kidney disease.
